subject: Next steps: VectorCloud A/B probe — latency & tokens/sec qualification
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-10-04T15:02:00Z
Subject: Recap: call with VectorCloud (CTO + Ops) — probe asks and risk signals

Quick recap of the call w/ VectorCloud (Sara Malik, CTO; Tom Lee, Head of Ops) — high level notes and recommended next steps: 

- Business / ask: they want a controlled, side-by-side A/B of Redwood vs their incumbent hyperscaler provider (HyperScale) focused on user-facing text-gen endpoints. Primary concern: tail latency under bursty traffic plus tokens/sec throughput for typical 1.5–4k token responses.
- SLA guardrails: VectorCloud indicated they need p95 <= 220ms and p99 <= 700ms for their 90% of production traffic; they're OK with slower tails for extreme long-run sequences but want to see comparative deltas.
- Key test scenarios they requested: steady-state 50rps (baseline), short bursts (200rps for 30s), long responses (3k tokens), and mixed small+large workloads to exercise batching.
- Instrumentation: they want per-request p95/p99, tokens/sec, and per-token CPU/GPU utilization traces if we can provide. Also asked for traceable request IDs for correlation to their logs.

Gaps / risk signals:
- They run a lot of multi-turn chat with context caching — need to validate KV-cache behavior and sequence-length optimizations.
- They care about cold-start microbursts (stateful model warmups).

Recommended immediate actions (owners):
1) Put together a concise Lab Spec (scope, datasets, traffic profiles, metrics + thresholds) — owner: Marissa; due: 48h (2029-10-06 COB).
2) Draft A/B runbook + required infra pieces (endpoint names, keys, sample payloads, request-id header) — owner: Ben; due: 48h.
3) Provide sample latency artifacts (p95/p99 snapshot, tokens/sec slide) and a short primer on how Redwood computes token accounting and KV caching — owner: Priyom; due: 72h.
4) Send proposed dates to VectorCloud and confirm whether they want Redwood-only isolation runs first or simultaneous side-by-side. — owner: Alex (me).

I'll pull together the initial lab-spec draft and loop the team into the external email. Thoughts on the p95/p99 target above? If we think 220/700 is unrealistic on their longer responses we should propose an agreeable threshold with justification.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Sara Malik <sara@vectorcloud.io>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@vectorcloud.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-10-04T16:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Next steps: VectorCloud A/B probe — latency & tokens/sec qualification

Sara / Tom — thanks again for your time today. Per our conversation, proposed concrete plan below: 

1) Scope: 3 test scenarios — (A) steady 50 rps 256-token responses; (B) burst test 200 rps for 30s with mixed lengths; (C) long-response test with 2.5–3k tokens at 5 rps to assess KV cache impact and throughput.
2) Metrics we will report: p50/p95/p99 latencies, median and 95th tokens/sec, per-request token counts, error rates, and GPU utilization sampled every 10s.
3) Test windows: suggested week of Oct 7–11 (UTC) — we can do Redwood-only isolation runs on Mon/Tue and side-by-side AB across HyperScale on Wed/Thu, with Friday reserved for triage. Please tell us which days work for you.
4) Deliverables from Redwood ahead of runs: Lab Spec (PDF), example payloads, short primer on our KV caching and batching behavior, and a sample latency CSV so you can see exact columns. Attaching a first-pass lab-spec and a sample CSV for context.

Action: can you confirm whether you want an isolation baseline first, or simultaneous side-by-side runs? If isolation, we'll target Oct 7. If side-by-side, we'll aim at Oct 9–10.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Attachments: VectorCloud_lab-specs.pdf (application/pdf), sample-latency-results.csv (text/csv)

From: Sara Malik <sara@vectorcloud.io>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@vectorcloud.io>
Date: 2029-10-04T18:41:00Z
Subject: Re: Next steps: VectorCloud A/B probe — latency & tokens/sec qualification

Alex — thanks, plan looks good. A few clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

- We'd prefer isolation runs first so we can baseline behavior without network/pathology differences. Please schedule Redwood-only on Oct 7 and the HyperScale comparison on Oct 9.
- For the tail analysis we want 99th-percentile measured both at request-completion and end-to-end from our LB (we'll send you a small agent to inject request IDs so we can correlate). Can you provide both RPC-level (your reported) and end-to-end (from our LB) timestamps?
- For throughput: please include tokens/sec computed both per-request and aggregated per-minute.
- Can Redwood share a short CSV example with the columns you'll provide? (p50,p95,p99,req_id,tokens,ts_start,ts_end,gpu_util). Your sample file looks promising but want to confirm column ordering.

Also, one ask: if we see p99 spikes > 1s on the long-response test, we'd like an on-call escalation path to a Redwood engineer during the Friday triage window. Who should we contact?

Thanks — Sara
Sara Malik
CTO, VectorCloud

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Sara Malik <sara@vectorcloud.io>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@vectorcloud.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-10-05T09:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Next steps: VectorCloud A/B probe — latency & tokens/sec qualification

Sara — perfect, isolation first it is. Quick responses to your asks plus owner assignments: 

- CSV schema: we'll provide the exact column ordering. Example columns (we'll send as CSV): req_id, model_variant, payload_tokens, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, ts_start_utc, ts_end_utc, tokens_per_sec, cpu_pct, gpu_pct, node_id. (See attached sample-latency-results.csv)
- Timestamps: Redwood can provide RPC-level start/end timestamps and a request_id header for correlation. We cannot directly instrument your LB but with the agent/request-id you provide we'll map end-to-end.
- Escalation: Priyom Das (cc'd) will be your triage lead for Friday. He can be reached at pri@redwood.com and on Slack (pri-ops). If p99 spikes > 1s we will page the infra team and join the triage call.

Owners + immediate deadlines: 
- Lab Spec (scope + traffic profiles + pass/fail): Marissa — draft by Oct 6 COB (attached draft).
- Runbook (endpoints, keys, payloads, request-id header): Ben — draft by Oct 6 COB.
- Sample artifacts and primer on KV-caching: Priyom — sample CSV and 1-page primer by Oct 7 AM.

I'll schedule Redwood-only on Oct 7 AM UTC and plan to share the orchestration details (endpoint names / keys) by EOD Oct 6.

On the escalation contact — Priyom will own Friday triage. Pri, please confirm availability (we need someone on-call Friday 14:00–18:00 UTC).

— Alex

Attachments: VectorCloud_lab-specs.pdf (draft), sample-latency-results.csv (sample)
